content_html:
House siding collects dust, pollen, splash marks, and biological growth, but wood, fiber cement, stucco, metal, and vinyl need different methods. Safe cleaning starts by identifying the material and using the least pressure needed without forcing water behind the cladding.

Identify the siding material and finish

Check home records or manufacturer guidance if you are unsure. Paint, sealant, joints, and material age all affect which cleaners and pressure levels the exterior can tolerate.

Start with water, a soft brush, and compatible cleaner

Work in small areas and, when the cleaner directs it, from bottom upward to limit streaking, rinsing before product dries. Protect plants and exterior electrical fixtures and do not mix cleaning chemicals.

Avoid forcing water into seams, vents, and windows

A strong jet can drive water behind siding or around window frames and create hidden moisture. Keep spray direction similar to natural rainfall where possible and reduce pressure around transitions.

Use professional access for high or fragile areas

Do not operate a pressure washer from a ladder where recoil can upset your balance. High elevations, deteriorated materials, or areas near overhead wiring require safer access and often professional service.
